headline: Surgical frequency decluttering of 250–800 Hz mid-mud, phase-aligned panning to fix negative stereo correlation, and front-to-back hall staging.
diagnosis: Severe 250–800 Hz low-mid mud accumulation across all calm and energy cues (e.g., calm-glowmoss hits 82.5% low-mid share; energy-glowmoss hits 62.3%), masking wind and string leads due to stacked octave-0 block-pad voicings.

Negative stereo correlation on all fast cues (battle at -0.11, energy-cascade at -0.11, energy-glowmoss at -0.08, energy-keep at -0.09, title at -0.01) caused by out-of-phase wide pads and unpanned divisi layering.
Squashed dynamics across all 10 loop Cues (1.2 dB DR on calm-glowmoss, 4.2 dB on battle) resulting from flat velocity stacks and absence of dynamic hairpin automation.
Unmanaged low-end collision in 60–250 Hz between Celli, Double Basses, Timpani, and Gran Cassa, causing phase cancellation and mud below 120 Hz.
global: Establish standard 5-part divisi seating pan staging: Violins I L35%, Violins II L15%, Violas R15%, Celli R35%, Double Basses C0%. Route section sends to FX1 (Grand Concert Hall) at -18 dB for front-desk leads, -12 dB for mid-sections, -6 dB for VELA/CANTUS pads.
Clear the 250–400 Hz lead vocal/solo wind corridor: voice pads with open-fifth/octave drop spacing, keeping no sustained inner-voice chords between C3 and F4.

Enforce low-end clarity rule: Double Basses (lyra-double-bass-arco) and low SOMA drums (timpani-32-profondo, concert-gran-cassa) strictly centered (Pan 0%), staggered rhythmically to avoid simultaneous transient spikes below 80 Hz.
Automate performDoc and track volume lanes across all cues with dynamic swells (p to ff hairpins over 2–4 bar phrases) to expand dynamic range from <4 dB to >12 dB.

title.verdict: Fix near-zero stereo correlation (-0.01) and 51.4% low-mid mud; create spacious orchestral front-to-back staging for the lantern motif.
moves: Pan Violins (lyra-silk-strings) L35%, Lead Horn (lyra-french-horn) C0%, Trumpet L10%, Flute R20%, Oboe R10% to eliminate negative phase cancellation in bars 0–24.
Drop String Pad register by one octave (C2–F3) and reduce gain by -4 dB to unmask the Lead Horn and Oboe in the 300–700 Hz band during bars 0–8.
Set lyra-harp ARP to Pan R30% with FX1 (Grand Concert Hall) send at -14 dB, giving high-frequency shimmer (2k–8k Hz) space away from central wind leads.
Automate volume swell on Timpani (timpani-29-dresden) roll in bar 15 from -18 dB to -2 dB with Gran Cassa impact at bar 16 beat 1 centered.

calm-glowmoss.verdict: De-congest catastrophic 82.5% low-mid share and 1.2 dB dynamic range into an airy, wide 3/4 waltz.
moves: Thin the sustained block pad (F3+A3+C4+G4): move inner voices to lyra-viola (Pan R15%) and lyra-cello (Pan R35%, octave C2–F3), cutting energy at 250–500 Hz.
Assign lyra-clarinet solo (bars 0–16) to Pan L10% dry (-22 dB FX1), and lyra-concert-flute solo (bars 16–32) to Pan R10%, carving a pristine central pocket for the melody.
Integrate tonos-kora (plucked ostinato) panned L25% running 8th-note broken arpeggios, adding pluck transients in the 1.5k–4k Hz band to compensate for the 0.014 presence band shortfall.
Add volume hairpin automation on lyra-silk-strings pad: swell from -24 dB (bar 0) to -12 dB (bar 8), dropping back to -20 dB (bar 16) to establish a 10+ dB dynamic range contour.

calm-cascade.verdict: Balance sub-60 Hz boom (15.7%) against high Lydian woodwinds, restoring stereo width from 0.33 to 0.65.
moves: Shift lyra-cello root notes down from octave -12 (D2–A2) to pure D1–A1 fundamentals, freeing the 150–300 Hz region for tonos-valiha and tonos-koto harp-like counter-patterns.
Pan Solo Violin (lyra-concert-violin, bars 16–32) to L20% with FX1 hall send at -16 dB; pan answering Oboe to R15%, creating spatial antiphon for the lantern motif.
Introduce tonos-koto (Pan R30%) playing 16th-note Lydian cascade figures (A5–C#6–D6–E6) wet (-10 dB FX1), adding pristine 4k–10k Hz air energy (currently sitting at a low 1.3%).
Automate performDoc rubato dynamics on Flute (bars 0–16) with expression swells on sustained notes (E6:2, F#5:3).

calm-keep.verdict: Carve out 66.1% low-mid mud to let felt piano and hushed choir breathe in moonlit space.
moves: Re-voice felt piano (lyra-felt) chords in bars 0–16: isolate root in left hand (D2–Bb1) panned C0%, voice right-hand triads above C4, eliminating chordal clumping between F3 and A3.
Position VELA choir pad (bars 16–32) wide across L45%/R45% with high-pass spacing above D3 and FX1 send at -8 dB, raising stereo correlation from 0.06 to +0.50.
Add tonos-nyckelharpa playing bowing accents on beat 1 of bars 16–32 (D3/A3), panned L20%, providing organic bow-noise texture in the 1k–3k Hz presence region.
Automate Solo Celli lead line (bars 16–32) dynamic wheel (CC1) from p (value 35) up to f (value 95) on peak D6 at bar 25.

energy-glowmoss.verdict: Eliminate phase inversion (-0.08 stereo corr) and 62.3% low-mid clutter in the 138 BPM gallop.
moves: Fix negative correlation: pan Spiccato Strings (lyra-string-quartet) L30%/R30% divisi instead of wide stereo-widened single track; pan Horns L20% and Trumpets R20%.
Replace sustained Trombones mid-register stabs with short staccato accents on beats 1 and 3, reducing sustained energy in the 250–500 Hz zone.
Add tonos-kamale-ngoni panned L25% playing syncopated 16th-note bass-line octave jumps (F2–F3), lock-synced with bodhran-kerry-tipper (Pan C0%) for clean low-end punch.
Apply automated dynamic dips (-3 dB) on string pads whenever Trumpets call the lantern motif in bars 16–32.

energy-cascade.verdict: Correct negative correlation (-0.11) and expand 4.9 dB dynamic range into a soaring Lydian gallop.
moves: Re-seat brass section: Horns L25%, Trombones R25%, Trumpets C0% (lead motif counter). Clear out out-of-phase FX2 delay feedback causing negative correlation.
Assign lyra-harp ARP sixteenths to Pan R35% paired with tonos-guzheng-glide panned L35%, creating a wide, sparkling high-frequency (2k–8k Hz) decorative frame.
Hollow out low-mid rhythm: shift pizzicato basses (lyra-pizzicato) to C0% octave D2–A2, leaving 300–600 Hz open for the Lead Horn gallop melody.
Automate Snare roll (orchestral-field-snare) in bars 15–16 and 31–32 with exponential volume curve from -24 dB to +1 dB for maximum section transition impact.

energy-keep.verdict: Clean up 64.2% low-mid buildup and negative correlation (-0.09) in the D minor castle gallop.
moves: Unstack heavy D minor chord voicings: drop Double Basses to D1, move Trombones up to octave D3–F3 (Pan R20%), and keep Spiccato Violins in octave D4–A5 (Pan L25%).
Introduce tonos-tar-knocking/tonos-hurdy-gurdy rhythm accents on beats 2 and 3 panned L30%, providing distinct mid-range bite without adding muddy sustained pad tone.
Route section percussion (SOMA bodhran + field snare) to a tight acoustic room send, keeping Gran Cassa strictly dry and center at 0% pan.
Automate dynamic crescendo from bar 1 to bar 16 (p to ff), expanding dynamic range from 6.1 dB to 14 dB.

danger.verdict: Tighten 39.4% low-mid share and focus scary 3/4 tension, enhancing presence and air above 2 kHz.
moves: Pan Tremolo Strings (tremolo-strings) L40%/R40% with high octave voicing (D4–F5), stripping away 200–400 Hz pad build-up.
Bring Solo Violin lead into Pan C0%, dry (-20 dB FX1 send), with Alto Flute (bars 8–16) panned R15%, creating a close-up, intimate foreground stage.
Layer tonos-hardanger fiddle playing sympathetic-string micro-swells behind the Bassoon counter-motif (bars 0–16), panned L20% with high presence detail (2k–5k Hz).
Set tar-nubian-deep heartbeat dynamics: bar 0–8 single stroke at -6 dB peak; bar 8–16 double stroke with second hit at -3 dB, centered at Pan C0%.

fear.verdict: Open up 53.6% low-mid frequency dominance; lift presence energy from 3.9% for intense 1 HP Phrygian panic.
moves: Isolate low Cello Phrygian melody (bars 0–16) to Pan C0%; move ticking pizzicato (lyra-pizzicato) to Pan R30% with tight mechanical velocity (no pad bleed).
Introduce tonos-sarangi with pitch-glides on the Phrygian Eb4 to D4 resolution panned L25%, adding evocative friction texture in the 1k–4k Hz zone.
Filter hushed VELA choir (bars 8–16) to high register (A4–F5), panned L35%/R35% wet (-8 dB FX1), rising stereo correlation above 0.50.
Automate sharp accent dynamic spikes (+4 dB) on Gran Cassa hits at bars 8 and 12, followed by immediate quiet decay to enhance peak-to-RMS contrast.

battle.verdict: Remediate critical phase inversion (-0.11 stereo correlation) and 52.8% low-mid mud in the Hollow Warden war-waltz.
moves: Eliminate negative phase correlation: un-group stereo brass/string pads. Pan Horns L30%, Trumpets R30%, Violins I L20%, Trombones R10%, Choir L40%/R40%.
Clear 250–500 Hz collision: remove low sustain from Trombones in bars 0–16; convert to short, sharp counter-punches on beat 1 and 3.
Add tonos-bouzouki-tremolo panned L15% doubling the fast violin gallop runs in bars 16–32, adding crisp high-mid transient bite (2k–6k Hz).
Balance SOMA drum low end: balance timpani-29-dresden (Pan L10%) against bendir-atlas-gut (Pan R15%) and concert-gran-cassa (Pan C0%), avoiding simultaneous sub-60 Hz frequency overlap.

clear.verdict: Preserve excellent 29.6 dB dynamic range while polishing high-frequency air and brass brilliance.
moves: Pan Trumpet C0%, Flute L15%, Violins R15%, Horns L25%, Trombones R25% across the 3-bar span to create an expansive victory arc.
Add tonos-santur glissando swell across bar 2 beat 4 into bar 3 beat 1 (Pan L30% to R30% sweep), adding sparkling presence (4k–10k Hz).
Ensure lyra-harp sweep in bar 2 reaches top register F6 without clipping, feeding FX1 hall send at -10 dB for a wide tail.
Set final Fmaj9 chord (bar 3) track volume decay envelope over 4 seconds, letting the Grand Concert Hall tail die out naturally to -60 dB.

gameover.verdict: Maintain stellar 40.5 dB dynamic range and +0.45 correlation while softening 64.3% low-mid heaviness.
moves: Keep felt piano (lyra-felt) front and center (Pan C0%), dropping left-hand accompaniment gain by -3 dB in the 200–400 Hz region.
Pan Oboe melody answer (bars 2–4) to R15% and Viola counter-line to L15%, separating them cleanly from the piano decay.
Layer tonos-dampers/tonos-kantele soft harmonic pluck on bar 4 final F major chord, panned R25% with -14 dB hall reverb.
Automate master fade-out starting at bar 3 beat 3 down to silence at bar 4 beat 4, protecting low-end tail from rumble.

mustKeep: The game-wide LANTERN MOTIF (sol·do–re–mi: C5·F5 G5 A5 in F major) and its minor/phrygian transformations across all cues.
The exact melodic lines of the three calm lullabies (calm-glowmoss, calm-cascade, calm-keep) loved by Kenne.
The exceptional dynamic range performance of clear (29.6 dB) and gameover (40.5 dB).
Seamless game-loop bar boundaries and pitch/tempo crossfade relationships across stage calm/energy/danger/fear states.
